headline: Hot CPI pushed the 10-year to 4.98% and Goldman now expects more Fed tightening, but CoreWeave's beat-and-raise has AI futures bouncing into Wednesday's open.
regime: The tape gave back Monday's bounce: Semis ETF -0.8% on the day, -6.7% on five days and -18.2% on the month, with the Nasdaq -8.0% on the month and in correction. The 10-year rose to 4.98% after a hot CPI, so rates are the ceiling on any rally. Every AI segment is down 14-32% on the month; only hyperscalers (+2.0%) and power (+1.4%) are positive on five days, while memory (-18.2%) and grid (-10.7%) led the fall. CoreWeave's print is lifting futures, but one earnings beat has not yet changed the trend.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Talen signed a seven-year 750 MW capacity agreement with an investment-grade counterparty (ac52a72cb2f3)
AAON jumped 22.7% as data-centre cooling sales rose 218% (67fa45f3b713); CoreWeave's contracted power passed 4.6 GW (d81825067750)
Against: Constellation's CEO says the US has 6-7 years of untapped power for data centres, so scarcity may be overstated (36bb33e0008f)
Against: SoftBank took a $3.7bn charge on power equipment and is reassessing its Ohio site; GE Vernova fell 4% (0a68be2242fd); grid is -10.7% on five days
theses.change_note: -3: Constellation's own CEO arguing power is not scarce and SoftBank's power-equipment write-off cut against the thesis, even with Talen's contract and AAON's orders.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: CoreWeave beat on revenue and raised its 2026 forecast to $13.3bn, with active power above 1.7 GW (d60ae3909efa, d81825067750)
TSMC's October sales rose 60% (cad2a5c934d9); OpenAI's revenue reportedly reached $10bn (b66c45db160a)
Netlist revenue rose 149% on AI demand (eff79dac6111)
Against: Super Micro's operating cash flow turned negative as receivables and inventory ballooned (9136df002da0)
theses.change_note: +4: CoreWeave's raise is the clearest end-demand data point in weeks and was the test named yesterday.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave's interest costs nearly tripled and it carries about $35bn of debt (d81825067750, 4f80da80ce16)
The screen still drops IREN, NBIS, CIFR, WULF, APLD and CRWV as cash-burners (shortlist)
Against: $9bn of planned customer prepayments eased debt concerns and neoclouds rallied (a0c0a3cc81ca, fcc978aa3962)
theses.change_note: -4: CoreWeave passed its earnings test and found a funding route that does not need banks; the debt load itself is unchanged.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Sandisk trades at 3x forward earnings with a 9% FCF yield after revenue of $11.0bn (shortlist, 1fad48666127)
ETFs bought a net $554.6m of Micron on Nov. 9 (7ccd9d888a5b)
Against: memory is -18.2% on five days and -31.9% on the month, still the worst segment; Sandisk -23.7% on five days (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -4: valuations are cheap but the tape keeps falling hardest here; cheapness is not a catalyst.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Hyperscalers are projected to spend $1.3tn on capex in 2027 (39f8f6c95f78)
Microsoft fell as Anthropic targets its Office business with new Claude tools (898a4d4fb65b, 2021b4900435)
Against: hyperscalers are +2.0% on five days, the best AI segment (digest segments)
theses.change_note: No new cash-flow data; the Microsoft drop is a competition story, not a capex one.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: CPI came in hot and Goldman now pencils in additional Fed tightening; the 10-year is 4.98% (4160f995b23e, digest tape)
Healthcare leads tech by the widest gap in 25 years as investors cut AI exposure (626065e51eeb)
Anthropic seeks up to $1.4tn in its IPO and an analyst calls it the core driver of the AI trade (637bf8a78f37, c69763969b95)
Against: futures rose Wednesday as CoreWeave's results eased AI fears (22210ec353c5)
theses.change_note: +3: the hot CPI realised yesterday's top risk, and hanging the trade on one IPO is a crowding sign.

theses.title: A Democratic Congress raises policy risk for data-centre build-outs
evidence: Dell fell 12% in a week on Texas data-centre moratorium fears (0ddbf008bd75)
Credo and Lumentum sank 14% in a week as the midterm sweep hit AI data-centre stocks (e7b5095116fe)
Against: still no law or moratorium has been passed (digest)
theses.change_note: +2: the 'moratorium, a ban' talk is spreading from cooling to servers and optics, though nothing is enacted.

theses.title: The Huang probe puts Nvidia, and China export rules, at risk
evidence: A Super Micro co-founder was charged with routing banned servers to China, and the Singapore firm involved ties back to Nvidia allegations (caf7c9d6932a)
Nvidia is -18.3% on five days, the worst compute name; Alibaba plans to list its AI chip unit (digest segments, 8f2392aec88c)
Against: ETFs added Nvidia on Monday and some call it a bad-news buy (eb0c78fc809a, 79fc84612534)
theses.change_note: +5: a criminal charge makes the smuggling story concrete, and the stock is still falling hardest in compute.

compute.note: AMD +6.5% and NVDA -18.3% on five days; rotation inside compute, not a floor.

foundry_equipment.note: TSMC October +60% and -24% on the month; equipment makers are cheap-ish at ~18-20x with fat margins.

memory_storage.note: -18.2% on five days and -31.9% on the month; 3x earnings has not stopped the fall.

networking_optical.note: ANET +8.9% while AAOI -24.5% on five days; policy fear hit Credo and Lumentum.

servers.note: -12.3% on five days; Dell on moratorium fears and Super Micro burning cash and tied to smuggling.

power_nuclear.note: +1.4% on five days and Talen's 750 MW contract; Constellation's 'untapped power' remark is the watch item.

grid_electrical.note: -10.7% on five days on SoftBank and policy fears, but Quanta raised guidance; orders, not sentiment, decide.

cooling_thermal.note: AAON cooling sales +218% and Vertiv raised guidance; segment +3.3% on the day.

datacenter_neocloud.note: CoreWeave passed its test, but interest costs nearly tripled and most names still burn cash.

hyperscalers.note: +2.0% on five days, but Microsoft faces a direct AI threat to Office.

ai_software.note: -7.8% on five days and -23.6% on the month; AI agents now threaten incumbents.

risks: More Fed tightening after the hot CPI could push the 10-year through 5%.
A Texas or federal data-centre moratorium would hit grid, cooling, power and servers at once.
Criminal charges in the smuggling case could widen into new China export curbs on Nvidia.
A weak Anthropic IPO would remove what analysts now call the core driver of the AI trade.
If power is less scarce than assumed (Constellation's view), power and grid premiums compress.
watch: Whether Wednesday's CoreWeave-led bounce holds through the close with the 10-year near 5%.
Nebius's Q3 report and any further neocloud prepayment deals.
Cisco's earnings for AI networking demand.
Fed speakers on the size of a December hike.
Any Texas legislative move on data-centre moratoria.
